en: The Jātaka: The Fifth Book of Birth Stories,
Chapter on the Arising of Color (Vaṇṇārohavagga)
5. The Ahituṇḍika Jātaka “I am a rogue,
my dear Sumukha, defeated at dice by the throw of the dice-stone.”
“Let us eat the mangoes from the tree;
we shall consume your vigor.
“Alas, my friend, you speak what is false to me!”
You praise with what is untrue;
who have you heard of, or seen,
a monkey named Sumukha?
Even now, O snake-charmer, that [incident] remains in my mind, when you,
having entered the grain market, [tried to harm me].
"Intoxicated, you wish to kill me who am hungry.
Therefore, even if I must endure a bed of suffering,
I would rather exercise sovereignty over the kingdom."
I would not give even when asked,
for I was terrified by fear; yet,
one who knows [the truth] is born into a noble family.
One who is content in their home and free from stinginess—
by that, a wise person is worthy of maintaining both companions and friends.
The Fifth Jātaka: The Snake-Catcher.
